serving_route: llama.cpp llama-server (OpenAI-compatible API, started on demand, never co-resident with nnU-Net/MoveIt GPU use), consumed by ~/claude-auto/claude_auto/localcoder.py
deletion_policy: Only the model selected in LLM-05's project benchmark is kept under models/llm/; the other candidates' GGUF files are deleted from local disk (not from Hugging Face) immediately after the LLM-05 benchmark run completes. No candidate GGUF is downloaded by this card (LLM-01) -- sizes/hashes below are taken from the Hugging Face API without downloading.

candidates.name: Qwen3.6-27B (Q4_K_M GGUF)
candidates.architecture: dense 27B, hybrid Gated-DeltaNet/Gated-Attention (16 of 64 layers are full attention; rest are linear/Gated DeltaNet)
candidates.vram_estimate_gb: 16.82 GiB weights + ~2.1 GiB KV @32K (only 16 full-attention layers, GQA 4 KV heads x256 dim) + ~0.5-1 GiB linear-attn state/compute buffers = ~19.5-20.5 GiB, fits 24 GB on-demand-exclusive
candidates.tool_calling: llama.cpp llama-server --jinja; base template has documented bugs (thinking-block handling, premature stops) fixed by community templates (froggeric/Qwen-Fixed-Chat-Templates, spiritbuun/buun-Qwen3.6-chat_template) layered on the official chat template via --chat-template-file

candidates.name: Laguna-XS-2.1 (Q3_K_M GGUF)
candidates.architecture: MoE 33B total / 3B active per token, 40 full-attention GQA layers (48 Q heads, 8 KV heads, head_dim 128), 256 experts / 8 active
candidates.vram_estimate_gb: 14.51 GiB weights + ~5.2 GiB KV @32K (dense GQA KV cache over all 40 layers) = ~19.7 GiB, fits 24 GB on-demand-exclusive. NOTE: the official poolside/Laguna-XS-2.1-GGUF release ships only Q4_K_M (20.27 GiB) and BF16; Q4_K_M + 32K KV (~25.5 GiB) exceeds the 24 GB budget, which is why the smaller bartowski Q3_K_M requant (imatrix, base_model:quantized:poolside/Laguna-XS-2.1) was selected instead
candidates.tool_calling: llama.cpp llama-server --jinja against the model's chat_template.jinja (vLLM/llama.cpp-compatible per model card); community jlens/chat-template forks exist (e.g. gghfez/Laguna-XS.2-jlens-GGUF) for reliability tuning, not required for basic tool calls

candidates.name: Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct (IQ4_XS GGUF)
candidates.architecture: MoE 30B total / 3B active per token, 48 full-attention GQA layers (32 Q heads, 4 KV heads, head_dim 128), 128 experts
candidates.vram_estimate_gb: 16.38 GiB weights + ~3.15 GiB KV @32K = ~19.5 GiB, largest headroom of the three (~4.5 GiB free for compute buffers)
candidates.tool_calling: llama.cpp llama-server --jinja; this model's native Hermes-style tool-call format is a long-established llama.cpp target (unsloth GGUF discussion documents chat-template + tool-calling fixes as of 2025-08-05)

considered_not_selected.name: Gemma 4 26B-A4B-it
considered_not_selected.reason: Hugging Face repo tags list license:apache-2.0, but Google's Gemma family has historically shipped under the separate Gemma Terms of Use (usage-restriction clauses, not plain Apache-2.0); the HF tag alone is not sufficient primary-source confirmation of an unrestricted license and needs the actual LICENSE/Gemma-Terms text checked before it can be a candidate. Deferred rather than spending part of the 3-candidate cap on an unverified license.
